headline: Global football crisis: AFC joins UEFA and CONCACAF in opposing FIFA plan
summary: The Asian Football Confederation warns of a possible World Cup boycott as FIFA proposes selling a stake in the World Cup's commercial operations.
details: The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has joined UEFA and CONCACAF in condemning FIFA's proposed private investment plan. The AFC expressed alarm that the situation has reached a point where a World Cup boycott is being publicly discussed.

The crisis deepened as Carlos Cordeiro, a senior advisor to FIFA president Gianni Infantino, resigned in protest. Cordeiro called the proposal a "bad deal for football" and the long-term future of the game.

FIFA's plan involves selling a stake in the business operations of the World Cup and Club World Cup through a commercial subsidiary, the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). The plan could raise up to $4.2 billion.
If approved, the plan would provide each of FIFA's 211 member associations with a one-off payment of $20 million in 2027 and increase their funding for the 2027-2030 cycle.
UEFA has taken a hard line, pledging that none of its national teams will participate in any FIFA competition as long as the proposal remains alive, stating that the World Cup is not for sale.
CONCACAF member associations have unanimously rejected the proposal. The European Union has also praised UEFA's stance in defending the integrity of the game.
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has defended the initiative as a "golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally."
FIFA maintains that it will proceed with an "open and democratic consultation" to ensure all member associations can vote based on facts.

headline: Powerful pressure-cooker bomb recovered in Ashulia
summary: Police defused a high-powered device containing bearing balls and explosives, left by a mysterious man outside a grocery shop.
details: Police recovered a powerful bomb concealed inside a pressure cooker from a locked bag left on a bench outside a grocery shop in Ashulia, on the outskirts of Dhaka.
The device was wrapped in black adhesive tape and was discovered after locals became suspicious of an unattended bag left outside Joyi General Store in the Khejur Bagan area.
A man aged between 30-35 was seen leaving the bag behind after he was told the shopkeeper had no change for a Tk 500 note while he was attempting to buy a soft drink.
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Bomb Disposal Unit safely destroyed the device in a controlled explosion at an open field in Amir Sarkar Housing.
According to the DMP Bomb Disposal Unit, the bomb was constructed with bearing balls and an explosive chemical compound, making it highly powerful.
Police are currently analyzing CCTV footage from the surrounding area to identify and locate the man who left the device.
This incident follows a similar discovery on July 24, where an improvised explosive device (IED) was found concealed inside an umbrella near Motijheel Metro Rail Station.
